ios.desc:
Malinois detects when someone handles your unattended iPhone, even someone who knows your iPhone passcode. Leave it on your desk, in a gym locker, or in a hotel room. The moment it detects movement, a screen touch, or a plug-in/unplug event, it writes a time-stamped record to the Event Log, then captures a photo or video when it can.

It's a detector, not a lock, built for one outcome: your iPhone will either be in the same state you left it, or you'll know it wasn't. Before you rely on it, turn on Guided Access with its Side Button option off; Malinois walks you through it.

HOW IT WORKS
Set a Malinois PIN, ARM, and set the device down. After a short grace period it calibrates its sensors and the screen goes dark: fully black on battery, so the phone looks off; dimmed on a charger, where the camera stays ready and iOS shows its recording indicator. Disarm anytime by pressing and holding the screen and entering your Malinois PIN.

TRIPWIRES YOU CONTROL
• Device motion — someone picks it up or shifts it
• Power / Cable — the charging cable is pulled or connected
• Touch — the screen is tapped or swiped (always on)
• Proximity — something approaches or covers it
• Sound (Pro) — a sudden sound nearby
• Vision (Pro) — movement in the camera's view while the camera is ready (on a charger by default)

EVIDENCE THAT SURVIVES
• Photo or video clips from the front camera, or the rear or both at once (Pro)
• Optional flash/LED so evidence isn't lost in the dark
• An Event Log of every arm, disarm, and trigger, with no way to delete a single entry, not even with your PIN. It keeps your most recent events and retires the oldest automatically; a Malinois that's been wiped is itself a sign that something happened
• Evidence you can export for building security or police
• Each event's upload to your PRIVATE iCloud starts before the photo is even taken, then the photo or clip (Pro, once iCloud access is verified, when online, with iCloud backup on), so a phone switched off seconds later can still leave its record behind

ALERTS ANYWHERE (Pro)
Get a "tamper detected" notification on your other Apple devices when it trips.

CHOOSE YOUR RESPONSE
• Alert — a silent on-screen warning
• Stealth — silently gather evidence
• Siren — an optional loud alarm to scare off an opportunistic snoop or intruder

BUILT TO RESIST TAMPERING
• PIN-locked disarm with brute-force lockout — Malinois can't be disarmed in the app without your PIN
• Guided Access is required to arm by default: wit

show_hn.title: Show HN: Malinois – Open-Source iOS Unattended-Device Tamper Detection

quotes.text:
Built for evil-maid/insider-access scenarios where your device passcode may be known.

Malinois’ singular objective is to guarantee, to the greatest extent possible, that you either return to an unattended device in the same state you left it, or know that unauthorized access was attempted (or succeeded).

With Guided Access on, Side Button option off, and iOS set to ask before new wired accessories connect, there is no viable scenario (short of an already compromised device) where a tamper can occur without an indication.

Designed around the iOS Guided Access feature, which is novel in the space as far as I can tell.  This solves the iOS backgrounding issue that relegated the Guardian Project’s now-defunct Haven app to Android, and though the app’s goal is different, a lot of the same functionality exists.

My goal with the post is feedback and hopefully some small, interested user base covering scenarios different from mine: This is a personal project, I am not an iOS developer, and the code is 100% Claude. My workflow is basically build with Claude, review and red-team with GPT/Deepseek/etc., then device testing with personal devices, and that can only take me so far.

I think the concept and GA differentiating it from existing apps is real, but I also think the models are a bit sycophantic when it comes to discussing that, and would love to have people smarter than me poking holes in my premises and assumptions, not to mention the code.
